findings.quote: After eleven years of sitting in morning traffic behind a school bus,
findings.note: Sixteen words before the main subject "I".
"The board" opens four consecutive sentences.

findings.quote: Given the results of the pilot and what both teams told us in the May retrospective,
findings.note: Seventeen words precede the main subject "I".

findings.quote: At a quarter past four on the ninth of March, Ellen Morrow
findings.note: The main subject "Ellen Morrow" arrives after 11 words of introductory phrase, plus the name itself brings the count to 12 words before the verb. The subject is Ellen Morrow.
"conduct" is an empty verb carrying the action noun "review"; the reviewing is done by the board.
"Made" is an empty verb carrying the noun "decision" instead of the verb "decide". The action is buried in the noun.
"Undertaking" is the action noun; the verb is the empty "given".
"Assessment" is the action noun; the verb is the empty "carry out".
"Determination" names the act that "determine" would express, and the verb carrying it is "makes".
The action is buried in the noun "realization" while the verb "had come to" does the work. The verb "realize" carries the same action.
"Expectation" names the act of expecting while the clause's only verb is "was".
"Observation" carries the act of observing under the empty verb "made".
"Evaluation" carries the action, while the verb is the light "carried out"; the root verb "evaluate" is buried in the noun.
"Expectation" is an action noun carried by "There was"; the acting party is absent.
The draft does not say who raised the concerns, and no actor is named in the surrounding sentences. The reader needs that actor to weigh the claim.
The clause does not say who made the decision in 2023, and the surrounding sentences name no actor.

findings.quote: Flood warnings for Quay Street were not issued
findings.note: The draft never says who was responsible for issuing flood warnings. The actor matters because the warning came too late to help the shops.
No one is named as having promised the sandbags, and the surrounding sentences do not identify them. The broken promise is the point of the sentence.
Doubled pairing: "plain and simple" says one thing twice. It also sits inside a clause that already contrasts "slower" and "faster".
"picturesque" repeats within three sentences; the first occurrence is in the preceding phrase about the row of Victorian houses on Linden Street.
Doubled pair: "full and complete" says one thing twice.

findings.quote: My bike was stolen in June. I bought a new bike and a new lock in July.
findings.note: "bike" appears in two consecutive sentences; the first occurrence is in "My bike was stolen in June."
"reviewed" appears a second time in this paragraph; the first occurrence is in "the board reviewed only changes on the high-risk list" two sentences earlier.
"cumbersome" appears twice in two sentences; the first is in "Its checklist is cumbersome for a one-line fix."
"oversight" appears twice in two sentences; the first is in "Nor is it an attempt to remove oversight from our release process."

findings.quote: I left the house at six-forty. I reached the bottom of the hill by seven. I arrived at my desk with wet socks and a temper.
findings.note: Three consecutive sentences use the same first-person past-tense template with a time or place slot. The first is "I left the house at six-forty."
"bus routes" appears here and again in the next sentence; the first occurrence is in the same sentence, before the quote.
"sodden" appears twice within two sentences; the first is in "the smell of sodden flour".
"whole" appears in the first sentence ("the whole street") and again in the second sentence ("the whole body"). The first occurrence is in the paragraph's opening sentence.

findings.quote: It is a feeling that recurs
findings.note: "It is a feeling" opens two consecutive sentences; the template repeats with only the final word changed.

findings.quote: It is a feeling that recurs.
findings.note: "It is a feeling that" repeats the identical opening of the previous sentence, used twice in consecutive sentences. The two sentences follow the same template and add no new structure.
"resolution" and the passive "was arrived at" repeat from the previous sentence's "a resolution would be arrived at" and "No resolution was arrived at."

findings.quote: The flood wall was built in 1962 and has been raised once, in 1991. Since the election, the council has given an undertaking to carry out an assessment of the flood wall
findings.note: "flood wall" is repeated in two consecutive sentences, the second occurrence inside the assessment sentence.
Doubled pair: "each and every" says one thing twice. The first half is "each".

findings.quote: It was decided by the committee that a decision would be made
findings.note: "decided" and "decision" share a root and sit in the same clause. The duplication is in the opening words.

findings.quote: and some lost things that are harder to put a price on
findings.note: The clause template "some lost..." runs three times in a row: "Some lost stock", "some lost income", "some lost things".
"a rule" appears twice in the same sentence, once before "you cannot switch off" and again immediately after.

findings.quote: There is no Accept button and no apply action.
findings.note: Two clauses built on the same "no X" template, saying the same thing about what the interface lacks.
"webdriverio" appears twice within two sentences; the first use is in the sentence beginning "webdriverio and the WebDriver plugin are for driving".
"Both" opens three consecutive sentences ("Both return", "Both filter", "Both start"), a template the paragraph gains nothing from.
"finding" appears a third time here within three sentences, after "replaces the finding" and "clear findings".
"major" repeats within two sentences; the first occurrence is in the preceding sentence ("Marking a revision major").
"stale" appears twice within two sentences; the first is in the list "open, addressed, dismissed, stale."
"findings" recurs within the paragraph; the first occurrence is in "including the answers with no findings."

findings.quote: a toll booth on the highway to production
findings.note: Empty figure. The image supplies no mechanism the literal claim about approval delays does not already carry, and it sits beside the stock figure in the next sentence.

findings.quote: an anchor that kept me moored to my own small concerns
findings.note: Mixed figure: a cocoon and an anchor cannot both hold in the same sentence, since one encloses and the other tethers. The two images cancel rather than combine.

findings.quote: without becoming a straitjacket that ties every team to the same Thursday
findings.note: Two figures crowd one sentence. "safety net" is a stock image, and "straitjacket" is a stock image for constraint, but the draft never says what constraint it means, so the sentence leaves the actual oversight mechanism unnamed.

findings.quote: A wave of support followed that lit a fire under the council.
findings.note: Mixed figure. A wave cannot light a fire; the two images in one sentence cannot both hold, and what the support actually did to the council is left unsaid.

The sentence opens on "On foot" and "the city", neither of which appeared earlier; the link to the previous sentence is carried only by the contrast at its end. The previous sentence was about the car as a cocoon and anchor.

findings.quote: Municipal snow contracts in our city specify

The previous sentence ends on a recommendation about extending lead approval to all product teams from the first of November. This sentence opens on the writer's own welcome of comments, which appears only here.
The previous sentence was about the board's checklist and weekly schedule; this one opens on unnamed concerns, a new element, before reaching the delays that connect it.

findings.quote: The handoff between the author and the board

The previous sentences are about the damage to the building; Tom is named here for the first time in this paragraph, with no earlier mention.

The previous sentence was about admission controllers rejecting a deploy. This sentence opens on the median wait for approval, which the paragraph has not introduced.

The previous sentences were about the app and text it does not insert. This sentence opens on "A finding", an element not mentioned before it.

The previous sentence is about Tauri wrapping the editor layers; 'Rust' appears here with no prior mention in the paragraph as the new subject.

findings.quote: Two months is a short period,
findings.note: The sentence opens on "Two months", a new span of time that nothing in the previous sentence prepared. The sentence before was about a lead approving a change they do not understand.

findings.quote: A safety net should catch mistakes

The sentence opens on a new element, content_text, which the previous sentence did not mention. The previous sentence was about content_json.
Opens on "The app", a new subject. The previous sentence was about the plugin and rfd.
